Sports.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales finish bottom of group
Sports.summary: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese football federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. Turn a new page and all that. This was a welcome victory for Jorge Jesus, for whom a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark a few days ago was a harrowing juncture, and there were plenty of positive takeaways for Wales, too. David Brooks cancelled out Bruno Fernandes’s pure opener from the edge of the box and then seized the lead through Sorba Thomas, who applied the finishing touch to a purring team move. But Neto, who picked up two bookings in one minutes and 59 seconds, the second for a foul on Brennan Johnson, equalised before half-time. Craig Bellamy’s side were fun and, at times, freewheeling but Forbs had the final say with a neat run and finish. Continue reading...

Sports.title: Rassie Erasmus’s tired ref-blaming act is wearing thin – South Africa deserve better | Robert Kitson
Sports.summary: Springboks’ achievements are remarkable but their head coach lacks statesmanship, diplomacy and good grace in defeat So here we go again. Exactly five years have passed since South Africa’s head coach, Rassie Erasmus, first felt the full force of World Rugby’s ire for criticising match officials. And guess what? This most habitual of offenders has just copped another lengthy ban – and deservedly so – for his latest intemperate comments, notable as ever for their total lack of statesmanship, diplomacy or good grace in defeat. To his acolytes his outspoken nature is part of what makes Rassie such a groot leier (great leader). To many others it simply cements his status as a serial prat. For the avoidance of any doubt everyone respects the remarkable achievements both of Erasmus and his double World Cup-winning teams. It is the rest of the package, sadly, that is too often a major letdown. Continue reading...

Sports.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
Sports.summary: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money.
